places.raw_name: the main trail to Texas from Fort Smith
places.name: Marcy Trail
places.note: Janey guides Roscoe west along the busy road, meeting soldiers, a big Missouri family, and two menacing outlaws as trees thin out.
places.location_hint: road from Fort Smith, Arkansas southwest across Indian Territory into north Texas

places.name: Gully where Roscoe was robbed
places.note: In a thunderstorm the outlaws Hutto and Jim strip and rob Roscoe; Janey pelts them with rocks until July arrives and captures them.
places.location_hint: open treeless plain in north Texas, half a mile north of the trail, not far from Indian Territory; about a night's ride from Fort Worth

places.name: Fort Worth
places.note: July delivers the outlaws to the sheriff, tells Roscoe in a saloon he will hunt Elmira first, and boards Janey at a livery stable.

places.name: July's camp north of Fort Worth
places.note: Camped amid trail herds; by morning Janey has followed them on foot and returns July's boarding money.
places.location_hint: about twenty miles north of Fort Worth on the plains, with trail herds bedded on both sides

places.name: Fort Smith
places.note: Roscoe misses its snug jail; soldiers on the trail are heading there.

places.name: Missouri
places.note: Home of a large wagon family heading west to farm.

places.name: Indian Territory
places.note: Hutto argues they are near it, so killing the travelers would go unnoticed.

places.name: Arkansas
places.note: Roscoe tells the outlaws they are from there; July suggests Roscoe take the children back.

places.name: East Texas
places.note: Hutto and Jim are known for robbing and sometimes killing settlers there.

places.name: Texas
places.note: Roscoe recalls Elmira's leaving is why he came into it at all.

groups.label: July Johnson's party
groups.at: July's camp north of Fort Worth
groups.hint: heading north onto the plains, a day or more beyond Fort Worth, searching for Elmira

groups.label: Hutto and Jim
groups.hint: handed over to the Fort Worth sheriff
